note: Two manually reviewed historical cases with individual FAA/DOT source receipts and clearly labeled uncertainty. No live status, flight telemetry or inferred shared root cause.

cases.title: FAA nationwide ground stop
cases.summary: The FAA temporarily stopped departures nationwide after instability in air traffic control telecommunications and radar data. The ground stop ended that evening; operational recovery continued into November 14.
cases.editorialNote: Historical, manually reviewed public-source snapshot. Not a live FAA status feed, flight manifest, current travel advisory, or definitive root-cause report.

sources.title: November 14: Airspace restoration and preliminary investigation

sources.publisher: FAA Air Traffic Control System Command Center
sources.title: ATCSCC Advisory 111: National Ground Stop

timeline.label: Communications and radar data instability
timeline.detail: In a November 13 briefing, the Transportation Secretary said inconsistencies at ATC centers and TRACONs began around 3:36 p.m. Eastern.

timeline.label: Nationwide departure ground stop
timeline.detail: FAA ATCSCC Advisory 111 was signed at 20:54 UTC (3:54 p.m. Eastern) and directed departures to remain stopped nationwide. This is the advisory signature time, not proof of the exact moment all operations stopped.

timeline.label: Airspace reopened
timeline.detail: Transportation Secretary Duffy reported that the airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern; departures were expected to resume gradually as crews and aircraft became available.

timeline.label: Operational recovery reported
timeline.detail: DOT said U.S. airspace was open again but passengers should anticipate delays and cancellations during the recovery.

timeline.label: Possible equipment or installation fault under investigation
timeline.detail: DOT described maintenance involving copper-to-fiber / TDM-to-IP migration and reported abnormal router connection attempts. Officials explicitly said the specific fault had not been determined. This is a preliminary account, not a settled root cause.

cases.comparisonNote: Two nationwide ground stops in different years. Public records describe different affected systems and separate investigations; similarities do not establish a shared technical cause.

cases.title: FAA NOTAM system outage
cases.phase: Ground stop lifted; remediation measures described
cases.summary: An overnight NOTAM-system outage disrupted the distribution of aviation safety information and prompted a nationwide departure stop on January 11, 2023. FAA officials later described preliminary database-related findings and corrective safeguards.
cases.editorialNote: Historical editorial snapshot based on official FAA statements and testimony. The causes described were preliminary at the time; this is not a live NOTAM status feed or an independent technical forensic report.

sources.title: FAA NOTAM statement and updates, January 11 and January 19, 2023
Acting Administrator Billy Nolen's Senate testimony on the NOTAM interruption

timeline.label: NOTAM services became unreliable
timeline.detail: FAA testimony says NOTAM applications and services became unreliable late January 10. Technicians tried switching to a backup database and activated stakeholder status communications.

timeline.label: Nationwide ground stop ordered
timeline.detail: In later Senate testimony, Acting Administrator Billy Nolen said he ordered a nationwide departure stop at approximately 7:15 a.m. Eastern while validation work continued.

timeline.label: Ground stop lifted
timeline.detail: FAA testimony states that the ground stop was lifted at 9:07 a.m. Eastern following system resilience checks. The FAA separately described a gradual return to normal operations.

timeline.label: FAA described preliminary file deletion finding
timeline.detail: The FAA reported that its preliminary review found contract personnel unintentionally deleted files during work on primary/backup database synchronization; it reported no evidence of malicious intent at that stage. The review remained ongoing.

timeline.label: FAA testified about added safeguards
timeline.detail: The FAA described introducing a synchronization delay between databases and requiring more than one person to oversee database work. The testimony still described the investigation as ongoing.

cases.comparisonNote: Both events led to nationwide departure pauses, but FAA sources describe NOTAM database issues in 2023 versus telecommunications/radar-data instability in 2026. Their root causes must not be conflated.
